name: The Garden Route
region: Western and Eastern Cape, south coast
tagline: A 300-kilometre stretch of lagoons, indigenous forest, wild beaches and mountain passes along South Africa's south coast, with bungee jumps, oysters and elephants.
highlight: The sea-carved cliffs and forest of Tsitsikamma, from the suspension bridge across the Storms River mouth.
shortDescription: A scenic coastal drive from Mossel Bay to Tsitsikamma, with Knysna's lagoon, Plettenberg Bay's beaches, ancient forests, the Storms River suspension bridge and the ostrich country of Oudtshoorn.
metaDescription: A Garden Route travel guide: Knysna and its Heads, Wilderness, Plettenberg Bay, Tsitsikamma and Storms River, Robberg, Oudtshoorn and Cango Caves, best time, how to drive it and a five-day plan.
knownFor: Lagoons, forests, beaches, adventure activities, oysters
goodFor: Road trips, coastal scenery, hiking, adventure, families

image.alt: The East and West Heads guarding the entrance to Knysna Lagoon

intro: The Garden Route runs for about 300 km along the south coast of South Africa, between the towns of Mossel Bay and Storms River, in a strip of land squeezed between the Outeniqua and Tsitsikamma Mountains and the Indian Ocean. Its name comes from the lush green landscape, in which lagoons, lakes, rivers, indigenous forest, fynbos and beaches follow one another, and it is one of the country's most popular tourist destinations.

The main towns each have a distinct character. Wilderness has lagoons and dunes, Knysna has a large lagoon with two rocky Heads at its mouth and a forest full of woodcarvers and cafés, Plettenberg Bay has some of the country's best beaches and the Robberg peninsula, and Tsitsikamma National Park has coastal forest, sea cliffs and a famous suspension bridge. Inland, Oudtshoorn is the ostrich capital, with the spectacular Cango Caves.

It is a place for driving, walking, kayaking and adventure. The Bloukrans Bridge has the world's highest commercial bridge bungee jump, whales and dolphins can be seen from the shore, and indigenous forests hold big yellowwood trees. It is a highlight of any South African trip, and best explored at a leisurely pace, with at least four or five days.

whyVisit.intro: The Garden Route is one of the great road trips in Africa, with beauty and variety at every turn.

points.title: Lagoons and forests
points.text: Knysna's lagoon and the Tsitsikamma forests are highlights.

points.title: Beaches and coves
points.text: Long, quiet beaches at Plettenberg Bay and Nature's Valley.

points.title: Adventure
points.text: Bungee, zip lines, kayaking, hiking and surfing.

points.title: Wildlife
points.text: Whales, dolphins, seals, monkeys, birds and elephants nearby.

points.title: Small towns
points.text: Craft shops, oysters and easy-going restaurants.

attractionsIntro: The route is best done with stops of a night or two in each area.

attractions.name: Knysna Lagoon and the Heads
attractions.text: A large estuary lagoon with two sandstone cliffs, the Heads, at its mouth. Boat trips, oyster farms and viewpoints make it the route's hub.
attractions.tip: Try a sunset boat cruise or fresh oysters.

attractions.name: Tsitsikamma National Park and Storms River Mouth

image.alt: The suspension bridge over the Storms River mouth in Tsitsikamma National Park

attractions.text: A coastal national park of forest and cliffs, with a 77-metre suspension bridge over the river mouth, walks, kayaking and the multi-day Otter Trail.
attractions.tip: Walk to the bridge in the morning.

attractions.name: Plettenberg Bay and Robberg
attractions.text: A resort town with white beaches, dolphins and whales offshore, and the Robberg Nature Reserve, a rocky peninsula with a seal colony and cliff-top walks.

attractions.name: Wilderness
attractions.text: A small village of lagoons, forests and long beaches, with kayaking, paragliding and a national park.

attractions.name: Bloukrans Bridge
attractions.text: A 216-metre bridge over a gorge with the world's highest commercial bridge bungee jump, and a walking tour under the arch.

attractions.name: Oudtshoorn and the Cango Caves

image.alt: Stalactites and stalagmites in the Cango Caves near Oudtshoorn

attractions.text: The centre of the ostrich industry in the Little Karoo, with farms and a spectacular limestone cave system, about an hour's drive inland from George.
attractions.tip: Book a caves tour, and visit an ostrich farm.

thingsToDoIntro: Outdoor activities and scenic stops fill the days.

thingsToDo.title: Walk to the Storms River suspension bridge
thingsToDo.text: A short coastal trail leads to a wobbly bridge across the river mouth.

thingsToDo.title: Kayak on the sea or a river

image.file: File:Tsitsikamma National Park (ZA), Kanus an der Küste -- 2024 -- 1990.jpg
image.alt: Kayaks resting on the rocky coast of Tsitsikamma National Park

thingsToDo.text: Paddle up a river gorge in Tsitsikamma or along the coast.

thingsToDo.title: Go whale and dolphin watching
thingsToDo.text: Boat trips from Plettenberg Bay from June to November.

thingsToDo.title: Do the bungee jump
thingsToDo.text: Leap from the Bloukrans Bridge if you dare.

thingsToDo.title: Eat oysters in Knysna
thingsToDo.text: The town is famous for its oysters, particularly during the Oyster Festival in July.
thingsToDo.tip: Try them fresh from the lagoon.

thingsToDo.title: Hike in the forest
thingsToDo.text: Trails such as the Otter Trail and shorter walks through indigenous forest.
thingsToDo.tip: Book the Otter Trail far in advance.

foodIntro: The Garden Route's food is seafood, dairy and local produce, served in relaxed restaurants.

foods.name: Knysna oysters
foods.text: Plump, briny oysters farmed in the lagoon.

foods.name: Ostrich meat
foods.text: Lean red meat, served as steaks and carpaccio.

foods.name: Farm stall lunches
foods.text: Homemade pies, cakes and jams at roadside farm stalls.

accommodation.intro: Choose from small towns along the route, with a night or two in each.

areas.name: Knysna
areas.text: Guesthouses and hotels around the lagoon.

gettingThere.intro: The Garden Route is best reached by hire car.

options.text: About 5 to 6 hours to Knysna, along the N2 highway.
Direct flights from Cape Town and Johannesburg.
About 2 to 3 hours to Plettenberg Bay.

gettingAround.intro: A car is best, though the Baz Bus links hostels.

options.text: A hop-on hop-off bus for backpackers.

bestTime.headline: November–April
bestTime.summary: The Garden Route has a mild, oceanic climate, with rain all year and warm summers.

seasons.text: Warm and sunny, and the busiest time.
Warm and calm, with fewer crowds.
Cool and wet, with whales and low prices.

bestTime.avoid: The Christmas and Easter holidays if you dislike crowds.

itinerary.title: Five days on the Garden Route

days.title: Wilderness
days.morning: Drive from Cape Town or George.

days.title: Oudtshoorn or Addo
days.morning: Cango Caves, or drive to Addo.
days.afternoon: An ostrich farm or a game drive.

tipsIntro: A few tips make the drive better.
tips: Book accommodation ahead for December and Easter.
Stay at least two nights in each area.
Drive in daylight, and be careful with livestock on roads.
Book the Otter Trail, Bloukrans and popular activities early.
Bring layers and a rain jacket.
Try oysters and local craft beer.

faq.q: How many days do you need for the Garden Route?
faq.a: Four or five days, with more if you add Oudtshoorn or Addo.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?

faq.a: It is the best way, though the Baz Bus and tours are available.

faq.q: Can I drive it from Cape Town in a day?
faq.a: Knysna is 5 to 6 hours away, but it is best to take it slowly.
